quotes.text: Remote Assist isn't a repair manual that hands you every answer. It's not a robot that diagnoses a machine on its own, and it definitely doesn't replace the trained person who has to do the work safely on site.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clears up the most common misconception about what Remote Assist does and does not do.

quotes.text: Each building block has a simple job. Teams connects people. Remote assist connects that conversation to physical work. Field service connects it to a planned service job and its history.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the architecture behind a remote support call in three crisp sentences.

quotes.text: Ask a simple question. Would an expert make a faster decision if they could see what the worker sees? If that view can prevent a delay or avoid an unnecessary trip, remote assist may fit the job well.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a practical test for deciding where Remote Assist is worth using.

quotes.text: No video call replaces lockout steps, protective equipment, approved work methods, or the judgment to stop when a situation is not safe.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States clearly that safety rules come before remote guidance.

chapters.title: A call from problem to guided fix
The building blocks behind the call

takeaways: Dynamics 365 Remote Assist lets a frontline worker share live video with a remote expert, who can mark the exact part or switch in the shared view.
Teams provides the calling and contacts, Field Service adds work order context, and Microsoft 365 with Entra ID controls who can join and access information.
Remote Assist fits visual, hands-on work where an expert's view prevents delays or trips, but it never replaces on-site safety rules or physical work.
hook: When a machine stops, the expert who knows it best is often far away, and photos, chats and phone calls leave too much to guesswork. This episode explains Dynamics 365 Remote Assist for maintenance, field service and operations teams. You learn how live shared video and on-screen guidance speed up fixes while people on site stay in control.
